newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanese judge demands death for 13 Islamists.
newsitem.headline: Lebanese judge demands death for 13 Islamists.

text.p: A Lebanese magistrate demanded the death penalty for 13 alleged members of a radical Islamist group after charging them with trying to assassinate two Moslem religious leaders and undertake acts of sabotage.
The 13 are suspected of belonging to a small Sunni Moslem militant Islamic faction known as Esbat al-Ansar (Band of Supporters).

Investigating judge Abdullah Bitar in an indictment demanded death for Ahmed Saadi and 12 followers for trying to assassinate Sheikh Taha Sabonji, religious leader of the northern city of Tripoli, in September 1994.

The 13, all Lebanese except Saadi and another alleged accomplice who are Palestinian, were also charged with trying to kill Sheikh Naji Taha, a member of of the pro-Syrian Ahbash Sunni Moslem group in November 1995 in Tripoli.
Saadi, known by the nom de guerre Abu Mohjen, and two others, including a Palestinian, are at large.

All 13 were also charged with trying to "attack state security by forming an armed group headed by Abu Mohjen that aims at evoking sectarian strife and urging sabotage acts and trying to blow up shops and establishments that sell alcohol in Tripoli".
No date has been set for the trial.

Abu Mohjen and 19 other followers -- 17 of whom are in custody -- are already standing trial on charges of belonging to a violent armed group and assassinating Sheikh Nizar al-Halabi, head of the Ahbash, in Beirut in August 1995.
